title: Exact straight-line flow windows had a higher winter mean rate across four Arctic gauges in 1980-2011
abstract: We counted exact nonzero constant-slope windows in ArcticGRO daily flow records. Thirty common years from 1980 to 2011 had complete certified January-March and July-September data at Ob, Lena, Yenisey and Mackenzie gauges. Seven-point windows were more common in winter by an equal-gauge mean of 5.90 percentage points. Conditional 95% three-year block limits were 4.62 to 7.27 points. Ob, Lena and Mackenzie had positive differences; Yenisey had little difference. Winter counts exceeded expectations from random order of each month's increments. Five- and ten-point checks retained a positive mean contrast. The result is consistent with known winter interpolation practices, but does not identify interpolated days or their error. Natural recessions, rounding, regulation, selected records and conditional uncertainty limit interpretation. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes, an arithmetic audit and a figure support reproduction. External daily records and record-level arrays remain outside the package.

display.caption: Exact seven-point windows by gauge and season. Black marks show the within-month random-order expectation. Error bars give conditional pointwise 95% three-year block limits.
